proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question specifies only a realized radius and an unnamed mixed experiment. It therefore does not determine the interval center, the deterministic split selector, or the actual laws and divergence conditions whose separation must match the modulus. The proposed claim narrows the question to the verified candidate and to the literal global-shift and localized-perturbation witness sequences used by the formal carrier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected open question must name the deterministic split selector and total-Gram center and must spell out the \(P_0\), \(P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), and \(P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) least-favorable witnesses underlying its first matching ratio.

proposed.justification: The question now names one fully explicit candidate: a deterministic admissible split sequence, the total-Gram center, and the exact realized-modulus radius. This makes coverage, expected full length, and the proposed sharp constant properties mathematically auditable for a single sample map and a specified mixed experiment.
proposed.gap: The proved order bounds do not select a deterministic split sequence or establish a joint sharp limit experiment. Fixed-design convex-modulus theory also does not settle uniform honesty of the zero-totalized radius, the moving random design under a merely measurable polynomial density envelope, or the three mixed regular-plus-local matching limits for the specified P0/Preg/Ploc witnesses.
proposed.consumer: A positive resolution would calibrate the shortest defensible full-length interval for a future atom-aware implementation of the same lower-threshold policy specification; a negative resolution would reject this explicit split-selected, total-Gram-centered candidate rather than the proved order-optimal interval.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether there exist one common sharp constant \(c>0\) and, for every admissible threshold sequence with a finite or infinite critical-scale limit, a deterministic data-independent split sequence \(B_{\bullet}\) for which the explicit total-Gram-centered modulus interval is eventually uniformly honest and all three ratios are matched by fixed-amplitude, bounded-product-chi-squared global and localized Bernoulli witness sequences.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen results prove only \(L_n^\star\asymp r_n\) and order-optimal honesty for the different bias-aware fallback interval. They do not provide the joint local asymptotic experiment, exact minimax constant, uniform integrability of the literal real-valued modulus handle in every higher-order regime, or a proof that zero radius on affine-infeasible designs preserves coverage.
obligation.attempted: The order-optimal upper and lower constructions, the phase decomposition, the exact realized-design modulus definition, and the verified global-shift and localized-perturbation witness predicates were compared. They control rates and bounded product chi-squared divergence but do not identify a common constant or certify the explicit modulus candidate's coverage; promoting either missing property to an assumption would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: Theorems \(\texttt{thm:honest-length}\) and \(\texttt{thm:phase-diagram}\) establish \(c r_n\leq L_n^\star\leq C r_n\) uniformly across the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes, and an explicit bias-aware atom-fallback interval attains the upper order. Theorem \(\texttt{thm:minimax-risk}\) supplies same-class global Bernoulli and localized Bernoulli witnesses with bounded product divergence at the two constituent rate scales.
